# Sidekick Realty and Estates: Colorado Real Estate Organized Around Four Situations

> Sidekick Realty and Estates is an independent Colorado brokerage owned by Nathan Van Camp. The practice is organized around four situations: buying or selling in Todd Creek Farms; selling rental, vacant, inherited, or investment property; relocating to Colorado; and relocating out of Colorado.

- Rental, vacant, inherited, and investment property sales: https://www.sidekickrealty.com/rental-vacant-properties

- Moving out of Colorado, for owners selling a Colorado home before leaving: https://www.sidekickrealty.com/relocating-from-colorado

## For employers and recruiters
Sidekick Realty and Estates offers a relocation resource for Colorado employers, recruiters, staffing firms, executive recruiters, and HR teams who recruit candidates from outside Colorado. Employers introduce a relocating candidate, and the candidate receives help with the housing side of the move: rental and apartment guidance, neighborhood and commute orientation, a rent versus buy discussion, home buying consultation and representation, and discussion of selling an existing home in another state. Initial relocation assistance is offered at no cost to participating employers, the employee is under no obligation to buy a home, and the employee is not required to use Sidekick Realty and Estates as their agent. Higher touch assistance can be discussed for executive and specialized hires. Page: https://www.sidekickrealty.com/employer-relocation

## Relocation to Colorado
Sidekick helps out of state buyers with market orientation, comparing communities against commute, price, property type, new construction, neighborhood character, outdoor access, schools, amenities, and work location; property searches; virtual tours; scheduling in person tours; offer strategy; inspection coordination; transaction management; and remote closing logistics. Buyers commonly relocate for new jobs, promotions, transfers, corporate relocations, new Colorado offices, and career opportunities.

## Relocation out of Colorado
Sidekick helps owners leaving Colorado sell a Colorado home, coordinating property preparation, contractors, cleaning, photography, showings, inspections, repairs, buyer negotiations, and closing from a distance. Sellers do not need to remain in Colorado during the transaction. Common reasons include job transfers, new employment, corporate relocation, promotions, retirement, and moving closer to family. Sidekick helps rental property owners across the Denver metro decide whether to keep or sell their property, including occupied rentals sold as-is with a tenant in place. Sidekick is also the neighborhood specialist for Todd Creek Farms, an acreage and large-lot community in Brighton, Colorado (80602).

## Who Sidekick Realty and Estates helps
- Rental property owners across the Denver metro who are weighing whether to keep renting or sell.
- Accidental landlords: people who inherited a home, or who moved and held onto the home they used to live in.
- Owners who want to sell a property with a tenant still living in it.
- Owners who want to avoid repairs, updates, cleaning, and repeated showings.
- Buyers and sellers of acreage and large-lot homes in Todd Creek Farms, Brighton 80602.

## The two ways to sell a rental property
- List on the market: the path to the highest price. The home goes on the MLS with full marketing so buyers compete for it. Typically the strongest final number, open to every buyer, and it involves showings and a normal closing timeline.
- Sell direct and as-is: the path of least disruption. Sidekick works with vetted direct buyers who purchase occupied rentals in as-is condition. No repairs, updates, or cleaning, and one walkthrough instead of repeated showings. This path usually nets less than a full listing.
- Sidekick will prepare both numbers side by side for a specific property at no cost.

## Common questions about selling a rental
- Can I sell with a tenant living in the home? Yes. Occupied rentals are sold all the time. Depending on the lease and the buyer, the home can sell with the tenant staying in place or after the lease ends.
- Do I have to wait until the lease is up? No. Some buyers specifically want a home with a tenant already in place, because the rental income starts the day they close.
- Do I have to make repairs or updates first? Not necessarily. Improvements can raise the sale price, but many owners sell as-is and skip the work.
- Will there be a lot of showings? A traditional listing involves showings. A direct sale can be done with one walkthrough, or sometimes none at all.

## Estate and inherited property in Colorado
- Sidekick Realty and Estates helps families and personal representatives sell inherited and estate-owned homes across the Denver metro.
- Whether a Colorado home must go through probate usually depends on how the deed was titled. Joint tenancy with right of survivorship, a beneficiary deed recorded before death, or a living trust can each transfer the home without probate. A home held in the deceased person's sole name generally requires probate.
- Colorado's small estate affidavit, set at $88,000 for deaths occurring in 2026, covers personal property only. It cannot be used to transfer real estate.
- A personal representative appointed in informal or formal probate generally has statutory authority to sell estate real estate without a separate court order, after receiving letters of appointment.
- Colorado has no state estate tax and no inheritance tax.
- Inherited property generally receives a stepped-up basis to fair market value at the date of death under federal law, so capital gains are usually calculated only on appreciation after that date.
- Inherited homes can be sold as-is with belongings still inside. Emptying the house is not required.
- Any one co-owner of a jointly inherited property can force a sale through a partition action in Colorado district court (C.R.S. 38-28-101 et seq.). Courts prefer physical division but will order a partition by sale when dividing a house is impractical.
- A sale of inherited property is reported as a long-term capital gain regardless of how long the heir held it, per IRS instructions for Form 8949.
- Colorado has a flat income tax rate of 4.4% for 2026 and taxes capital gains as ordinary income at that rate, with no reduced long-term rate.
- Colorado has no statute requiring a seller to complete the standard Seller's Property Disclosure form, but sellers have a common law duty to disclose latent material defects they actually know about. That duty still applies to a personal representative, measured against what they actually know.
- An inherited home can be sold as-is either by listing it on the open market in current condition or by selling direct to a vetted as-is buyer. Listing as-is often nets more; a direct sale is less disruptive.
- This is general information, not legal or tax advice.

## Key facts about Todd Creek Farms
- An all-ages neighborhood of large-lot, acreage homes with Brighton (80602) addresses, located in unincorporated Adams County.
- Served by a community well system rather than individual private wells; many homes use septic.
- Distinct from Heritage Todd Creek, which is a separate 55+ gated golf community with Thornton addresses.
- Recent sale prices generally range about $900k to $1.3M (mid-2026).
- About 20 minutes to Denver International Airport via E-470, and about 30 minutes to downtown Denver.
- Served by Brighton-based School District 27J.
